record: A software release on 7 December left a report-export link of the Learning platform & content reachable without sign-in, and it was used from an unknown address to download student records. The export reads the records decrypted, so encryption at rest did not protect them. The platform was taken offline to stop the downloads.
Student names, ages and schools; Assessment scores
regimes: Breach notification: 72h to supervisory authority (GDPR Art.33)
Breach notification: All 50 states have breach laws (typically 30–60 days)
Breach notification: SEC 8-K within 4 business days of materiality
DPDP — detailed report to the Board
Breach notification: Notify Board and affected principals without delay; detailed report within 72h
Cyber / sector law: CERT-In Directions 2022 — 6h incident reporting
phases: Before any incident: this policy and its playbooks, the tabletop exercises of Section 4, the IR retainer
Section 6.1 step 1, Detect & report: the event is logged in the incident tool and given a severity
Section 6.1 step 2, Triage, and the notification assessment of Section 6.2: confirm, scope, rate the risk, decide who must be told
Section 6.1 steps 3 to 5: Contain, Notify, Eradicate & recover
Section 6.1 step 6, Post-incident review: root cause, lessons, actions
Section 3.1 and Section 7.1: logs preserved, times in UTC, one incident timeline, chain of custody
events: The Amsterdam office holds its annual incident tabletop exercise, on a student-data leak, and updates its incident playbook.
Regional security monitoring detects an unusual number of student-record exports from the Learning platform & content to one unknown address, and reports it to the service desk.
The service desk logs incident INC-2610-3001 in the incident tool and gives it severity SEV2.
The IR team takes the Learning platform & content offline and blocks the unknown address, so that no more records can leave.
The Incident Response & Crisis Manager confirms that about 4,500 student records were taken, scopes the students' countries and starts the notification assessment.
IT closes the export link, restores the platform from a clean build and puts it back online under closer monitoring.
The DPO rates the risk to the students and decides which authorities and which people must be notified.
The DPO sends the notifications to the authorities, signed off by the General Counsel.
The post-incident review finds the root cause, a release that left the export link open, and gives the release checklist and the developers' training new actions.
bcdr: Business continuity: keeps the business running
plan: Student names, ages and schools; Assessment scores; about 4,500 records; children's data
INC-2610-3001 is recorded in LearnTech's breach register with this plan, by the DPO (BKB-POL-014 Section 6.2, step 4).
